req.title: Create schema on startup
req.statement: The system shall create the tasks table via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-024 requires that the tasks table is created via SQLAlchemy metadata at application startup. The key observable effect is that after importing the app (which triggers models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)), the tasks table exists and the API endpoints that depend on it respond correctly. Tests cover: (1) positive — root endpoint returns 200 with exact payload proving app started cleanly; (2) positive — GET /tasks/ returns 200 with a list (table exists and is queryable); (3) negative — POST /tasks/ with missing required field (title=null) returns 422 proving schema validation is active; (4) boundary — POST /tasks/ with title at max length 100 chars is accepted (201), title at 101 chars is rejected (422), catching off-by-one mutations on the schema constraint; (5) state-transition — after startup, creating a task and then retrieving it by id returns exact fields, proving the table is writable and readable end-to-end.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_root_endpoint_returns_200_with_exact_payload():

    r = client.get("/")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert body["message"] == "Welcome to Task Manager API"
    assert body["docs"] == "/docs"
    assert body["version"] == "1.0.0"

tests.name: test_startup_table_writable_create_and_retrieve_task
preconditions: FastAPI app imported in-process, create_all() called
tasks table exists and is writable
actions: POST /tasks/ with valid title and completed=false
expected: POST returns HTTP 201 with exact title and completed=false
GET returns HTTP 200 with same id, title, completed=false
trace: R-TASK-024: table created at startup must be writable and readable
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_startup_table_writable_create_and_retrieve_task():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Startup test task", "description": None, "completed": False}
    r_create = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r_create.status_code == 201
    created = r_create.json()
    assert created["title"] == "Startup test task"
    assert created["completed"] == False
    assert "id" in created
    task_id = created["id"]
    r_get = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    fetched = r_get.json()
    assert fetched["id"] == task_id
    assert fetched["title"] == "Startup test task"
    assert fetched["completed"] == False

test_startup_table_writable_create_and_retrieve_task()
